text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- Two Swiss right wing parties, the Swiss Democrats and the Lega, said that they support a referendum which demands that admission talks between Switzerland and the European Union must receive the approval of the Swiss population.
- The number of Swiss building permission requests has picked up in April for the first time this year.

- Peter Bodenmann, leader of the Swiss Social Democrats, said the success of Tony Blair's 'New Labour' party may not be easily transferred to Switzerland. Bodenmann critizised Blair's programme as 'wishy-washy'.

- Former security guard Chistoph Meili, who became famous as he saved bank documents from Union Bank of Switzerland's paper shredder, is going to the U.S. He hopes to meet his "friends Senator D'Amato and representatives of the Jewish World Congress."
- Swiss pension fund managers said that they will introduce a codex to fight misuse.
- Pro European activists said that they would withdraw a public initiative on Switzerland's joining the so-called European Economic Area (EEA). Swiss citizens rejected the EEA in December 1992.
